assessment: The goldfish names board density as the binding axis: 3.345 bodies by turn 6 against goblin-storm's 5.26. So the ten favours cards that add bodies per cast, multiply the metronome, or back up the two one-card classes the sim priced (Selvala drawn 12.2% by turn 6; one Craterhoof, the overrun kill drawn 42.7%). The audit's two UNDER axes — sweepers at 0 and no graveyard answer — each get a pick the measure can actually see. The last two slots are the bracket-4 door: Springheart Nantuko and Nissa, Resurgent Animist sit in the build's own pool file, held out of the 99 by the bracket-3 target because they carry recorded two-card infinites.

ten.why: Radagast discounts and flashes the first creature spell each turn, but on 5 mana you bank for one ambush per round; Muse untaps your lands in every untap step, so all four turns of a cycle cast a full-price body.
ten.unlocks: Up to four metronome casts per round instead of one — the straightest multiplier on the 3.345-bodies-by-t6 figure, and it turns Ohran Frostfang's and Toski's per-body triggers into a per-turn stream.

ten.why: The sim declares Selvala a one-card class, drawn 12.2% by turn 6, with no functional backup in the 99; Henge is the backup — a draw per nontoken body plus {G}{G} a turn, and any power-4 metronome creature already on board discounts it to five mana.
ten.unlocks: A second repeatable gas engine that also ramps, so losing Selvala or Beast Whisperer no longer stalls the draw plan.

ten.why: The audit reads sweepers UNDER at 0 and the goldfish's declared blind spot is that almost nothing blocks fliers; Whiptongue destroys every flier on ETB, wears a reach body, and Radagast flashes it for {3}{G} after attackers are declared.
ten.unlocks: The one sweeper the taxonomy credits that is also a flash trap — a board wipe the ambush plan can cast on an opponent's combat.

ten.why: Five bodies from one card against a deck averaging 3.345 by turn 6; stack 003 showed Craterhoof at X=6 clears 40 damage where X=5 does not, and Queen alone is five more X counts — flashed via Radagast for {2}{G}{G}{G}.
ten.unlocks: Board density and flier defence in one slot: five flying deathtouch blockers answer the exact attack the deck currently cannot block.

ten.why: Interaction-breadth reads UNDER with graveyard the one uncovered class (0 answers detected); Ooze answers it a card at a time with {G} activations, which is exactly what a draw-go deck holding mana open wants to spend it on.
ten.unlocks: The uncovered class gets a repeatable answer on a body that grows — against a reanimator or Loam opponent it is a threat and a hoser at once.

ten.why: OVERRUN ASSEMBLED — finisher plus a second wave — is 37% by turn 6 mostly for want of the wave; on this 36-land base Avenger makes six-plus Plants at once, and every Cultivate afterward pumps them.
ten.unlocks: The widest single injection of overrun fodder the colour prints; one Avenger turn makes any Stampede or Ibex swing lethal.

ten.why: The overrun class is four copies drawn 42.7% by turn 6 with one true Craterhoof; a fifth copy is the redundancy the deck's own kill-gap arithmetic (stack 003: a fifth body or a second finisher) asks for, and Radagast's discount flashes it in after blocks.
ten.unlocks: A second Craterhoof-shaped ending that arrives at instant speed — the ambush deck's version of a combat trick that wins the game.

ten.why: Radagast's flash covers only the first creature spell each turn and dies to one removal spell; Yeva gives every green creature spell flash, so the draw-go posture survives the commander being answered twice.
ten.unlocks: Commander insurance that deepens the engine instead of shielding it — with both out, the second and third creatures of a turn also ambush.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite landfall triggers; infinite tapped land tokens

ten.why: Held out of the 99 by the bracket-3 target because the combo index records a two-card infinite with Tireless Provisioner, who is already in the deck — sleeving it moves the computed floor from 1 to 4, and it sits in the build's own pool file.
ten.unlocks: The bracket-4 door: bestow it on any body and every land drop makes a copy or an Insect — value at bracket 3 tempo, an infinite with Provisioner if the pod ever asks for 4. The line needs a stack scenario before it is claimed as a kill.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite landfall triggers; infinite tapped land tokens

ten.why: The other half of the benched pair, also in the pool file: alone it moves no measured axis (ramp already reads OVER) and no bracket signal fires — its recorded infinite needs Springheart, so it only matters if both come in together.
ten.unlocks: Mana on every land drop plus an Elf or Elemental to hand on the second — and, paired with Springheart, the second key to the bracket-4 door. Unverified until a stack scenario runs the loop.

gaps: Ezuri's Predation is the true creature sweeper for this deck in Magic terms — a wipe that leaves you 4/4 bodies — but card_roles.json tags it only threat:tokens, so the sweeper axis cannot see it; a role-pattern addition or a read of the card at buy time settles which of it and Whiptongue Hydra the slot really wants.

Endurance (flash, reach, exiles a graveyard on ETB) misses the ten for the same reason from the other side: it carries no hate:graveyard role, so the interaction-breadth measure would not move — Scavenging Ooze took the slot because the measure credits it, not because Endurance is the worse card in a flash deck.

The spawning brief calls Springheart Nantuko and Nissa, Resurgent Animist Game Changers; cards.csv flags game_changer false for both. Their bench reason in the bracket engine is the two-card-infinite signal, and that is the framing used here. If the GC list has moved since the last extract, a pipeline refresh settles it.

The Springheart + Tireless Provisioner line is the combo index's record and the index is format-agnostic; whether the loop's mana actually closes in this 99 needs a /resolve-stack run before anyone shuffles it up at bracket 4.

Seedborn Muse moves the computed floor to exactly the target (3, via the Game Changer signal) — within bracket, but a GC in a deck whose floor was 1 is a pod conversation the numbers cannot have for the pilot.
